name: ANSI/IEEE spark gap symbol
summary: IEEE-oriented spark gap drawn as two facing electrodes separated by an air gap, which breaks down at high voltage.
description: A spark gap is a pair of electrodes separated by a gap that flashes over when the voltage exceeds its breakdown level. It appears in surge protection of telecom and control circuits and on older equipment as coordinating gaps. The publisher's IEEE miscellaneous preview lists a spark gap form, the counterpart of the existing IEC page.

This illustration is independent and not the IEEE graphic. A plain spark gap can sustain follow current after breakdown on power circuits, which is why power arresters use other technology. The breakdown voltage depends on gap spacing and conditions, and must be specified.
readingNotes: Check whether follow current could be sustained on the circuit.
Read breakdown voltage from equipment data.
drawingChecklist: Show the protected and earthed sides.
Use an arrester where follow current is a risk.
distinction: A spark gap is a simple breakdown element; a gas discharge tube encloses the gap in gas for a defined breakdown.
